sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: ______ and ______ are fundamental sectors of development in which specialists must utilize media to educate rural communities.
questions.answer: Agriculture; health.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: ______ and Health were the topics covered in the programmes broadcast under SITE.
questions.answer: Agriculture (and Family Planning); family planning.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Traditional media are closest to people needing development messages. (ii) Comics should be created by outsiders.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – they should be created locally.

questions.q: Name any two groups involved in development communication.
questions.answer: Voluntary organizations, NGOs, concerned citizens, development agencies (any two).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Define development communication.
questions.answer: The use of communication to promote development, i.e. to change or improve social and economic conditions of people.

questions.q: What was SITE?
questions.answer: Satellite Instructional Television Experiment (1975) that carried education and development programmes to 2400 villages.

questions.q: Why are street theatre and comics used for development communication?
questions.answer: They are participatory, in local language and culture and explain sensitive topics simply, e.g. hygiene and HIV/AIDS.

questions.q: Give two examples of development campaigns.
questions.answer: The monthly polio immunization day and the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the role of a development communicator.
questions.answer: A development communicator explains development to people so that it is accepted: understands development and communication, knows professional techniques and the audience, and prepares messages that are received, understood and applied.

questions.q: Discuss the use of radio, television and print in development communication.
questions.answer: Rural radio programmes since the 1940s, Doordarshan's Krishi Darshan and SITE, and newspapers writing on Five Year Plans carried development messages.

questions.q: List any five core areas of development and the sources of expertise.
questions.answer: Agriculture, fisheries, animal husbandry, education, health; expertise from agricultural colleges, state departments, Primary Health Centres and NGOs.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the term 'development communication' using examples.
questions.answer: It is the use of communication to promote development: radio programmes for farmers, street theatre on nutrition, comics on HIV/AIDS and polio campaigns; communicators design messages for the audience to accept and apply.

questions.q: Discuss the use of different forms of mass media in development communication.
questions.answer: Radio (rural programmes), television (Krishi Darshan, SITE), print (development themes after the Five Year Plans) and traditional media (street theatre, comics) work with agencies, NGOs and citizens.
